newsitem.title: UK: NWE high sulphur fuel oil sinks again on supply.
newsitem.headline: NWE high sulphur fuel oil sinks again on supply.

text.p: NWE high sulphur fuel oil barges sagged again on Monday because of good supply and little room in ARA to store incoming material, traders said.
High sulphur barges traded at $91, $92 and $92.50 fob ARA. Bids then rose slightly to around $92.50/$93 in what traders said was a correction to the earlier losses.
These prices compare to deals on Friday at as high as $98.

Dealers said that while oversupply and high inventory rates were the primary factor behind fuel oil's weakness, additional downwards pressure was coming in the short term from players who were pricing cargoes coming into NWE from outside the region.
High sulphur cargoes were notionally weaker alongside crude oil and barges.

Utility buyers said they had not seen specific new offers so far but suggested they would not be looking hard at the marker until later in the week, in the hope that the sloppy supply situation would filter through into yet lower cargo prices.
Low sulphur fuel was softer too, alongside crude. At least three cargoes are thought available from northwest Europe around the middle of the month.
